payload.document_summary: Synthetic narrative: a warehouse employee with approximately four years' service was dismissed on 3 March 2026 for 'gross misconduct' shortly after raising written health and safety concerns. The narrative states no investigation meeting was held, raising both ordinary unfair dismissal (procedure) and a potential protected-disclosure dimension.

drafter.factual_summary: The claimant, a warehouse employee of around four years' standing, was summarily dismissed on 3 March 2026 for alleged 'gross misconduct' shortly after raising written health and safety concerns. No investigation meeting or disciplinary hearing was held before the decision.

legal_framework.authority: British Home Stores Ltd v Burchell
Iceland Frozen Foods Ltd v Jones
legal_framework.citation: Iceland Frozen Foods Ltd v Jones [1982] UKEAT 0062_82_2207

legal_framework.authority: Polkey v AE Dayton Services Ltd
legal_framework.citation: Polkey v AE Dayton Services Ltd [1987] UKHL 8

application.facts_supporting: No investigation meeting was held, so the employer cannot show it formed its belief in misconduct on reasonable grounds after a reasonable investigation.
The complete absence of a hearing or appeal points to a procedurally unfair dismissal; any 'would have dismissed anyway' argument goes to a Polkey reduction in remedy, not liability.
Dismissal closely following protected health-and-safety concerns raises a question over the true reason, which is fact-sensitive and to be tested in evidence.

remedies.basis: s119 ERA 1996 — calculated on age, length of service and a week's pay.
s123 ERA 1996 — loss flowing from the dismissal, subject to the statutory cap for a pre-2027 EDT and to any Polkey reduction.
ss113-116 ERA 1996 — available but rarely ordered; the claimant should indicate preference.

drafter.overall_assessment: The unfair dismissal claim is arguable and, on procedure, strong. The principal exposure is evidential — establishing the true reason for dismissal and rebutting any band-of-reasonable-responses defence.

attacks.weakness: Qualifying service and reason may be contested; gross misconduct, if proven, is a potentially fair conduct reason.
attacks.legal_basis: s98(1)-(2) ERA 1996; band of reasonable responses
attacks.citation: Iceland Frozen Foods Ltd v Jones [1982] UKEAT 0062_82_2207

attacks.weakness: Even if the procedure was flawed, compensation may be heavily reduced if dismissal was inevitable on the facts.
attacks.legal_basis: Polkey reduction to the compensatory award
attacks.citation: Polkey v AE Dayton Services Ltd [1987] UKHL 8

factual_gaps.missing_fact: Whether any investigation, hearing or appeal occurred at all (the narrative asserts none, but the employer's records are not before us).
factual_gaps.why_it_matters: Determines whether the Burchell reasonable-investigation limb is breached.

factual_gaps.missing_fact: The precise content and audience of the health and safety concerns raised.
factual_gaps.why_it_matters: Goes to whether there is a qualifying protected disclosure capable of making the dismissal automatically unfair.

procedural_risks.risk: Time limit: three months less one day from the EDT (pre-October-2026 regime).
procedural_risks.consequence: A late ET1 is liable to be struck out unless it was not reasonably practicable to present in time.

procedural_risks.risk: ACAS Early Conciliation not yet shown as commenced.
procedural_risks.consequence: An ET1 presented without a valid EC certificate will be rejected.

critic.overall_vulnerability_assessment: The unfair dismissal claim's procedural footing is solid but its value is exposed to a Polkey reduction and to a conduct-reason defence. The protected-disclosure angle is promising but presently under-evidenced.

legal_test_completeness.reasoning: All s98 elements identified and addressed; minor gaps on qualifying-service evidence.

evidential_sufficiency.reasoning: Procedural unfairness is well-supported; the true reason for dismissal is under-evidenced.

procedural_compliance.reasoning: Correct time-limit regime and ACAS EC identified; EC certificate not yet obtained.

era_2025_awareness.reasoning: Correctly applies the pre-commencement regime to a March 2026 EDT and flags the upcoming changes.

authority_quality.reasoning: Authorities (Burchell, Iceland Frozen Foods, Polkey) are real, binding/persuasive and correctly applied.

judge.synthesis: The unfair dismissal claim is viable. The strongest ground is procedural unfairness (no investigation, contrary to Burchell), with the principal contest being the true reason for dismissal and the size of any Polkey reduction. On the rubric the argument scores 79/100 and crosses the 70-point viability threshold.
key_vulnerabilities: A conduct-reason defence if the employer can evidence reasonable grounds and investigation.
A Polkey reduction substantially cutting the compensatory award.
The protected-disclosure angle is currently under-evidenced.
evidentiary_requirements: Disclosure of the investigation and disciplinary records (or proof none exist).
Contemporaneous evidence of the health and safety concerns raised and to whom.
Pay and continuity records to fix qualifying service and quantum.
procedural_recommendations: Commence ACAS Early Conciliation immediately and preserve the certificate.
Calculate and diarise the three-months-less-one-day limit from the EDT.
Request written reasons for dismissal under s92 ERA 1996.
